item.buck_voltage_mode.C.name: Output capacitance
item.buck_voltage_mode.C_esr.desc: Resistance R_esr in series with C1. Blank = 0 Ω (ESR not simulated)
item.buck_voltage_mode.C_esr.name: Capacitor ESR
item.buck_voltage_mode.Kd.desc: Duty per volt-per-second of error change, through a first-order filter with time constant Tf
item.buck_voltage_mode.Kd.name: Derivative gain
item.buck_voltage_mode.Ki.desc: Duty per volt-second of integrated error, with anti-windup
item.buck_voltage_mode.Ki.name: Integral gain
item.buck_voltage_mode.Kp.desc: Duty per volt of output-voltage error
item.buck_voltage_mode.Kp.name: Proportional gain
item.buck_voltage_mode.L.desc: Output inductor L1, between sw and out
item.buck_voltage_mode.L.name: Inductance
item.buck_voltage_mode.R_load.desc: R1. With a load step, the value before the step
item.buck_voltage_mode.R_load.name: Load resistance
item.buck_voltage_mode.R_load_step.desc: At t_load_step the load changes from R_load to this value. Enter it together with t_load_step. Blank = no load step
item.buck_voltage_mode.R_load_step.name: Load after the step
item.buck_voltage_mode.Tf.desc: Blank = a quarter of the control period (auto)
item.buck_voltage_mode.Tf.name: Derivative filter time constant
item.buck_voltage_mode.Vin.desc: DC voltage of V1 (also used for Vleg = duty × Vin in the averaged model)
item.buck_voltage_mode.Vin.name: Input voltage
item.buck_voltage_mode.Vref.desc: With a reference step, the value before the step
item.buck_voltage_mode.Vref.name: Output voltage reference
item.buck_voltage_mode.Vref_step.desc: At t_ref_step the reference changes to this value. Enter it together with t_ref_step. Blank = no reference step
item.buck_voltage_mode.Vref_step.name: Reference after the step
item.buck_voltage_mode.d_max.desc: 0 to 1. You can also enter a percentage, such as 90%
item.buck_voltage_mode.d_max.name: Maximum duty
item.buck_voltage_mode.d_min.desc: 0 to 1. You can also enter a percentage, such as 90%
item.buck_voltage_mode.d_min.name: Minimum duty
item.buck_voltage_mode.f_ctrl.desc: How often the PID runs. A measurement reaches the command after one control period
item.buck_voltage_mode.f_ctrl.name: Control frequency
item.buck_voltage_mode.f_sw.desc: PWM carrier frequency. Must be a whole multiple of f_ctrl
item.buck_voltage_mode.f_sw.name: Switching frequency
item.buck_voltage_mode.fidelity.desc: Switching: S1 and S2 are ideal switches with on-resistance r_on (ripple is shown). Averaged: S1 and S2 are replaced by a duty × Vin source Vleg in series with the on-resistance Rleg (r_on), and the switching-period average is computed (no ripple, about 1/20 of the steps)
item.buck_voltage_mode.h.desc: Auto: the switching period ÷ 200 (÷ 10 for the averaged model)
item.buck_voltage_mode.t_end.desc: Auto: 20 × the LC resonance period (added to the last step time, if any), rounded up to a whole number of control periods
item.buck_voltage_mode.t_load_step.desc: Rounded up to the start of a switching period. Enter it together with R_load_step
item.buck_voltage_mode.t_load_step.name: Load step time
item.buck_voltage_mode.t_ref_step.name: Reference step time

notice.N-BIG-CHANGE.fix: Check that this is the value you meant. Here m is milli and M is mega.
notice.N-CONN-RESTART.fix: Run again to see the waveforms.
notice.N-CONN-RESTART.what: The app was restarted, so the results are gone. Your spec and edits are still here.
notice.N-DATA-FETCH.fix: Try again. If it keeps happening, run the simulation again.
notice.N-EXPORT-FAIL.fix: Check the free disk space and export again.
notice.N-MISSING-PAIR.what: {symbol} ({name}) has no value. It goes together with {pair}.
notice.N-MISSING.fix: Enter a value in the Spec panel.
notice.N-OPEN-ENCODING.fix: Re-save it as UTF-8 in a text editor.
notice.N-OPEN-LEGACY.fix: Check the values and units in the Spec panel. Saving writes them in the version 0.2 form (value, unit, source).
notice.N-OPEN-LEGACY.what: This spec uses version 0.1, so the control values have no units or sources. They were read in each item's unit: {list}
notice.N-OPEN-MULTI.fix: Choose the one spec JSON you want to open.
notice.N-OPEN-MULTI.what: {n} files were dropped. Only one can be opened at a time.
notice.N-OPEN-READ.fix: Check that the file hasn't been moved or deleted, then choose it again.
notice.N-OPEN-SCHEMA.fix: Fix the places listed below. Save a sample to see the format.
notice.N-OPEN-SCHEMA.what: {file} doesn't match the spec format ({n} place(s)).
notice.N-OPEN-SIZE.fix: Check that you chose a spec JSON.
notice.N-OPEN-SIZE.what: {file} is too large ({size}). A spec JSON can be up to 10 MB.
notice.N-OPEN-SYNTAX.fix: Check commas, quotes and brackets near that position.
notice.N-OPEN-TEMPLATE.what: This app has no template named "{template}".
notice.N-OPEN-TYPE.fix: This version opens spec JSON files only. Save a sample to see the format.
notice.N-OPEN-VERSION.fix: Update the app, or rewrite the spec in version {supported}.
notice.N-OPEN-VERSION.what: {file} uses spec version {found}. This app reads version {supported}.
notice.N-PLOTS-FULL.fix: Hide another signal to free a plot.
notice.N-PLOTS-FULL.what: There can be up to 4 plots. {signal} can't be shown.
notice.N-PREFS-SAVE.fix: Check that the settings folder ({path}) can be written to (permissions, free space). After fixing it, change any preference to save again. This notice goes away once they're saved.
notice.N-PREFS-SAVE.what: Couldn't save your display preferences (language, theme, panel sizes, and so on) to the settings file. They still apply on this page, but may not be kept the next time circuit-sim starts.
notice.N-REF-RANGE.fix: Check the reference, or d_min, d_max and Vin.
notice.N-REF-RANGE.what: {symbol} {value} is outside what the duty limits allow ({low} to {high}, ignoring losses). The output can't reach it.
notice.N-RUN-CIRCUIT.fix: Check the Spec panel for extremely large or small values.
notice.N-RUN-CIRCUIT.what: Run {n} failed: the circuit equations can't be solved with these values.
notice.N-RUN-DIVERGED.fix: Use a smaller time step and run again. For circuits with control, check the gains too.
notice.N-RUN-DIVERGED.what: Run {n} failed: {signal} stopped being finite at t = {t} (diverged).
notice.N-RUN-INTERNAL.fix: If it happens again with the same values, report it with the spec JSON and the details.
notice.N-RUN-INTERNAL.what: Run {n} failed: an unexpected error occurred.
notice.N-RUN-MEMORY.fix: Use an earlier stop time or a larger time step.
notice.N-RUN-MEMORY.what: Run {n} failed: the simulation is too large for the available memory ({steps} steps).
notice.N-RUN-NOTE-ROUND.fix: To avoid rounding, choose a time step that divides the step time evenly.
notice.N-RUN-NOTE-ROUND.what: The step time of {id}, {t}, was rounded to {t_grid} to fit the time step.
notice.N-RUN-NOTE-STEP.fix: Use a time step of {h_suggest} or less and run again. Leave it blank to go back to the automatic value.
notice.N-RUN-NOTE-STEP.what: In run {n}, the time step {h} was coarse for this circuit's fastest time constant ({tau}); the waveforms may be inaccurate.
notice.N-RUN-STEPS.fix: Use an earlier stop time or a larger time step. Keeping the time step, the stop time can be up to {t_max}; keeping the stop time, the time step must be at least {h_min}.
notice.N-RUN-STEPS.what: Run {n} didn't start: the step count is {steps}, over the limit of {limit} for one run.
notice.N-RUN-SWITCH.fix: Use a smaller time step and run again.
notice.N-RUN-SWITCH.what: Run {n} failed: the switch and diode states didn't settle at t = {t}.
notice.N-SAVE-INVALID.fix: Fix the input, then save again.
notice.N-SAVE-INVALID.what: Values with input errors ({list}) were saved with their last valid value.
notice.N-SIGNALS-FULL.what: Up to 8 signals can be shown at once.
notice.N-STALE.fix: Run again to see waveforms for the current values.
notice.N-STALE.what: The scope shows a result computed before you changed the spec (run {n}).
notice.N-STEP-AFTER-END.fix: Use an earlier step time or a later stop time. A blank stop time extends past the step automatically.
notice.N-STEP-AFTER-END.what: {symbol} {t} is after the stop time {t_end}, so the step won't appear.
notice.N-STEP-COARSE.fix: Use a time step of {h_suggest} or less. Leave it blank to go back to the automatic value.
notice.N-STEP-COARSE.what: The time step {h} is coarse for this circuit's fastest time constant ({tau}); the waveforms may be inaccurate.
notice.N-STEP-SNAP.fix: To use the exact time, make it a whole multiple of the switching period ({t_sw}).
notice.N-STEP-SNAP.what: {symbol} {t} will be rounded up to {t_grid}, the start of a switching period.
notice.N-STEPS-LIMIT.fix: Use an earlier stop time or a larger time step. Keeping the time step, the stop time can be up to {t_max}; keeping the stop time, the time step must be at least {h_min}.
notice.N-STEPS-LIMIT.what: The step count is {steps}, over the limit of {limit} for one run.
notice.N-UNIT-CONVERTED.fix: Check that the values in the Spec panel are what you intended. Saving writes them in base units.
notice.N-UNIT-CONVERTED.what: Values written with prefixed units were converted to base units: {list} (e.g. L: 47 uH → 4.7e-5 H)
notice.N-UNIT-WRONG.what: The spec JSON gives "{text}" for {symbol} ({name}). This item is in {unit}.
notice.N-UNUSED.fix: Remove them from the spec JSON if they aren't needed. Saving keeps them as they are.
notice.N-UNUSED.what: This template doesn't use these values: {list}. They are ignored in the simulation.

signal.buck_voltage_mode.cmd(duty).desc: Duty command (PID output, d_min to d_max, updated every control period)
signal.buck_voltage_mode.gate(q1).desc: Gate signal of S1 (1 = on, 0 = off)
signal.buck_voltage_mode.gate(q2).desc: Gate signal of S2, the complement of q1 (no dead time)
signal.buck_voltage_mode.i(L1).desc: Inductor current, positive from sw to out. Switching-period average in the averaged model
signal.buck_voltage_mode.i(V1).desc: Current through V1, positive from + to − inside the source (negative while V1 delivers power)
signal.buck_voltage_mode.i(Vleg).desc: Current through the averaged-model source Vleg (in series with Rleg between sw and 0), positive from + to − inside it. Equal to −i(L1) in this circuit
signal.buck_voltage_mode.v(out).desc: Output voltage at node out. Switching-period average in the averaged model
signal.buck_voltage_mode.v(sw).desc: Voltage at the switch node sw, including the drop across the switch on-resistance r_on. In the averaged model, the switching-period average duty × Vin − r_on × i(L1)
